newsitem.title: UK: Aerospatiale sees positive H1 result.
newsitem.headline: Aerospatiale sees positive H1 result.

text.p: French state-owned SNI Aerospatiale expects to post a first-half profit when its board approves the accounts later this month, a company official said on Sunday.

Finance director Francois Auque told journalists ahead of the Farnborough air show that the group's first-half results would be 'positive' and it was on its way to meeting its target of breaking even in 1997 and returning to profit in 1998, assuming an exchange rate of five francs per dollar.
The first-half accounts are due to be approved on September 18.
Auque announced the group's first-half sales of 23.1 billion francs and orders totalling 29.6 billion. He gave no year-ago comparisons.
Aerospatiale detailed for the first time the operating results contributions from each of its branches, including its 38 percent share in the Airbus Industrie consortium.

Aerospatiale's return to profit will be due to a current restructuring plan, which aims to find three billion francs of savings, its dollar hedging policy and a pick up in deliveries in the coming years of long-range Airbus jets, on which it makes the most money in the product family, Auque said.

He said the group was hedged at five francs per dollar and every 10 cents appreciation above that level translated into an additional profit of 300 million francs. At June of this year, the dollar was at 5.58 francs, he said.

Aerospatiale posted full-year 1995 sales of 49.2 billion francs and orders of 39.3 billion. It made 1995 net operating profit of 639 million francs but posted a net attributable loss of 981 million due to 1.5 billion in provisions for a restructuring plan running from 1996 to 1998.
